System Integrity Protection stops malware from changing macOS itself. It should never be off on a normal Mac. Turn it back on from Recovery mode with “csrutil enable”.
Gatekeeper checks that apps come from identified developers and were scanned by Apple before they open. With it off, any downloaded program can run without a warning.
FileVault encrypts your disk. Without it, anyone who takes your Mac can read your files by removing the disk or starting from another drive.
The firewall blocks unwanted incoming connections, for example on a café or hotel Wi-Fi. Turning it on doesn’t slow anything down and doesn’t affect your normal browsing.
XProtect is Apple’s built-in malware scanner. Its definitions look out of date; keep automatic security updates on so it learns about new threats.
Automatic security updates install fixes for actively exploited holes, often within days. Turn on “Install Security Responses and system files”.
